packages.title: Reconcile the preview with current development
packages.exit: A current isolated checkout contains the intended changes, has a reproducible local runtime and records its own passing baseline.

packages.title: Architecture and product contracts
packages.exit: Reviewed ADRs define ownership, capability enforcement, event delivery and extension boundaries with migration examples.

packages.title: Product design, localization and accessibility
packages.exit: Each delivery has reviewed FA/DE/EN flows, Iranian-calendar behavior, responsive evidence and keyboard-accessible states.

packages.title: Shared connector lifecycle and provider SDK
packages.exit: Two test providers exercise the same ownership, credential, refresh, reconnect, health and removal contracts without feature-specific bypasses.

packages.title: Events, rules and reliable delivery
packages.exit: A committed CRM event produces a traceable delivery; rollback, retries, duplicate jobs and revoked permissions have tested outcomes.

packages.title: Slack notifications and management
packages.exit: A local deal or activity change matches an active rule, produces a safe message and shows its delivery history, including outage and permission-loss cases.

packages.title: Slack commands, actions and unfurls
packages.exit: Signed Slack interactions resolve to a verified CRM actor, enforce permissions and produce auditable, safely scoped results.

packages.title: MCP and application authorization
packages.exit: A read-only grant cannot mutate through any tool, UI action or direct request; revoked or reduced access stops on the next request.

packages.title: Complete the CRM MCP capability surface
packages.exit: The capability matrix maps every supported workflow to tools, scopes, validation, failures and tests; unsupported operations are explicit.

packages.title: ChatGPT, Claude and supporting client apps
packages.exit: Local conformance passes for every claimed client profile; live installation and rich UI support are recorded separately per host.

packages.title: Mail integration hardening
packages.exit: Existing mail flows remain intact and multi-account or shared-mailbox changes follow explicit ownership and migration rules.

packages.title: Calendar domain and event workflow
packages.exit: Event creation/editing, recurrence, permissions and communication decisions have explicit semantics and round-trip correctly across calendars and time zones.

packages.title: Google Calendar and Google Meet
packages.exit: Synthetic changes converge between CRM and a local Google simulator; a separate live gate verifies the claimed account capabilities.

packages.title: Microsoft 365, Outlook and Teams
packages.exit: Selected Microsoft resources use the common lifecycle and show tenant/permission constraints with documented synchronization semantics.

packages.title: Zoom conferencing
packages.exit: Meeting creation, update and cancellation are tied to the correct host account and remain consistent with the CRM event.

packages.title: Public API and signed webhooks
packages.exit: Scoped API clients can perform documented operations and consume authenticated, retryable events without bypassing CRM visibility.

packages.title: Workflow and automation integrations
packages.exit: A workflow can react to a CRM event and call an integration action with traceable permissions, variables, retries and cancellation.

packages.title: Additional provider delivery tracks
packages.exit: Every released provider has its own supported workflows, local contract tests, localized management flow and live qualification record.

packages.title: Application SDK and isolated extension runtime
packages.exit: A private example app can add authorized data/UI/workflow capabilities, run in real isolation, update and uninstall without bypassing core policy.

packages.title: Marketplace and app management
packages.exit: A private app can be discovered, reviewed, installed, configured, updated and removed; public listing adds verified ownership and publication operations.

packages.title: Self-hosting, observability and operations
packages.exit: Operators can start required services, diagnose failures, rotate secrets, restore data and suspend delivery with documented evidence.

packages.title: Shared verification and release acceptance
packages.exit: Every released capability has reproducible source, runtime, authorization, localization and provider evidence appropriate to its claimed support level.

packages.title: Open-source distribution and maintenance
packages.exit: A contributor can reproduce the local setup, add a provider safely and understand which releases and integrations are actually supported.
